seal.checks.not: It is a seal of the server that made the file, not a signature of the people who signed.

seal.time.clock: The time in it is this server's clock.

seal.status.off: Not being applied right now, so documents completed now are made without it. Nothing else stops. The people who run this server have been told why.

rules.title: Sign-in rules
rules.intro: What everyone on {account} needs to sign in. With nothing set here, each person chooses for themselves.
rules.load_failed: We could not load the sign-in rules. Reload the page to try again.
rules.password.label: Shortest password
rules.password.hint: From {lo} to {hi}. It applies when someone chooses a password. Someone whose password is shorter is asked for a longer one the next time they sign in with it.
rules.idle.toggle: Sign out after a time of no use
rules.idle.label: Sign out after
rules.idle.hint: From {lo} to {hi} minutes. Two minutes before, the page says so and offers "Stay signed in". Signing pages of your documents check their link again after a break this long.
rules.one.label: One session at a time
rules.one.hint: When someone arrives in {account} in another browser, the browser they used before is signed out of it. API keys are not affected.
rules.one.confirm: Switching this on now signs out every extra browser of people who are signed in to {account} more than once. This browser stays signed in.
rules.two_step.on: Two-step login is asked of everyone.
rules.two_step.off: Two-step login is each person's own choice.
rules.leak.on: Every new password is also looked up in a list of passwords from data leaks, and refused when it is there. Only the first 5 characters of a fingerprint of the password leave this server. When the list does not answer within 3 seconds, the password is allowed.
rules.why.summary: Why there is no forced password change and no rule about capitals or digits
rules.why.body: NIST, the standards body of the United States, advises against both (SP 800-63B). People who must change a password every few weeks, or fit one to a pattern, choose weaker ones and write them down. A longer password, the check against leaked passwords and two-step login do more.
rules.code.label: Your code from your authenticator app, or a recovery code
rules.saved_out: Saved. {count, plural, one {# other browser was} other {# other browsers were}} signed out.
rules.owner_short: Your own password is shorter than {min} characters. As the owner you are not held by this rule, but choose a longer one under "Your sign-in" above.
rules.refused.password: Shortest password: type a whole number from {lo} to {hi}. It is still {kept}.
rules.refused.idle: Sign out after: type a whole number of minutes from {lo} to {hi}, or switch the rule off. It is still {kept}.
rules.password.too_short: Use a password of at least {min} characters.
rules.password.too_short_team: Use a password of at least {min} characters. {account} asks that of everyone on its team.
rules.password.leaked: This password has appeared in a data leak. Choose another one.
rules.password.gate: {account} asks everyone on the team for a password of at least {min} characters, and yours is shorter. Choose a longer one first. Until then nothing else in {account} opens for you. Your other workspaces are not affected.
rules.short.title: Choose a longer password to open {account}
rules.short.body: {account} asks everyone on the team for a password of at least {min} characters, and the one you signed in with is shorter. Choose a new one here and you carry on at once. Nothing was lost.
rules.short.forgot: Signed in another way and do not know the password? Sign out and use "Forgot password" on the sign-in page.
rules.short.failed: Something went wrong. Nothing was changed.
rules.warn.text: You will be signed out in {left}, because {account} signs out a browser that is not used for {count, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}.
rules.warn.failed: We could not reach the server, so we could not keep you signed in. Check your connection and press it again.
rules.left.minutes: about {count, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}
rules.out.idle: You were signed out because this browser was not used for a while. That is a rule of your team. Sign in to carry on where you were.
rules.out.elsewhere: You were signed out here because you signed in on another browser, and your team allows one session at a time. Sign in here to use this browser instead.
rules.away.checked: You were away for a while, so we checked the link again.
